reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the first three premises for a specific SLM-processed HEA, but provides no evidence for the fourth premise that the same mechanism applies to the chemically and structurally distinct (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, nor for the fifth premise that caloric performance is preserved. The hypothesis over-extrapolates from a single alloy system without direct support for transferability or functional compatibility.
premises: Slow cooling after solution treatment can induce serrated grain boundaries in high-entropy alloys.
Serrated grain boundaries increase tensile fracture strain and ductility by distributing strains more evenly and resisting intergranular cracking.
The serration mechanism involves coarsening of precipitates that pin and undulate grain boundaries during cooling.
The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy can form serrated grain boundaries via the same slow-cooling mechanism.
Serrated grain boundaries will not interfere with the field- or pressure-induced caloric phase transformations.
